candidates.title: Export leads to CSV
candidates.body:
Export every lead to a CSV file, so owners can open their pipeline in a spreadsheet or back it up.

## Requirements

1. **CLI:** `python3 leadgen.py export` writes CSV to stdout, so this works:
   `python3 leadgen.py export > leads.csv`
   - Use the stdlib `csv` module. No third-party dependencies (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
   - The first row is a header. Include **every column of the `leads` table**, in table order. Read the
     columns from the database (for example `PRAGMA table_info(leads)` or `cursor.description`), not
     from a hard-coded list, so columns added later are exported too.
   - One row per lead, ordered by `id`.
   - Multi-line fields (research, pitch, brief...) must stay in one cell: let `csv.writer` quote them.
   - Show `export` in the usage text (the module docstring at the top of `leadgen.py`).
2. **Download link (optional, welcome):** a "Download CSV" link on the Leads page served at
   `GET /leads.csv`, with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and
   `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="leads.csv"`. Build the CSV with the **same function** as
   the CLI. Don't write the logic twice.

## Security checks (required)

- `GET /leads.csv` must go through the existing `ok_origin()` check in `do_GET`, like every other route.
  Don't add a route that skips it: this file holds every lead's contact details.
- **CSV formula injection:** lead data comes from the web. Any cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`,
  a tab or a carriage return must be prefixed with a single quote `'`, so Excel or Sheets doesn't run it
  as a formula. Example: `=HYPERLINK(...)` becomes `'=HYPERLINK(...)`.
- Don't log or write the export anywhere except stdout or the HTTP response.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 leadgen.py export` prints a header plus one row per lead, with all `leads` columns.
- [ ] A lead whose notes span several lines round-trips through `csv.reader` unchanged.
- [ ] A cell starting with `=` is exported with a leading `'`.
- [ ] If the download link is added: `/leads.csv` returns 200 with a CSV attachment, and 403 when the
      `Host` header is foreign (the same check as `test_cross_site_and_rebinding_blocked`).
- [ ] No new dependencies; `leadgen.py` stays a single stdlib-only file.
- [ ] README mentions the command (CLI section) and CHANGELOG has an `Unreleased` entry.

## Testing

- Add tests to `tests/test_leadgen.py` (they use a temp DB and never call Claude). Cover:
  - the header and column set;
  - the multi-line round-trip;
  - the formula-injection prefix;
  - the `/leads.csv` 200/403 cases, if you add the route.
- Run `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v` locally. CI (ubuntu and macOS, Python 3.11 to 3.13) must
  be green on the PR.

## Out of scope

Import from CSV, filtering the export by status, and other formats (JSON, XLSX). Open a separate issue
if you want one of these.

candidates.title: Add CSV output for spreadsheets
candidates.body:
Many IT teams track domains in Excel. A `--format csv` option would make it easy to paste results into a spreadsheet or attach them to a ticket.

**Suggested behavior**
- One row per domain and check: `domain,check,status,detail`.
- Use Python's built-in `csv` module so commas and quotes in `detail` are escaped correctly.
- Print to stdout like the other formats, so `domaincheck -c domains.toml -f csv > report.csv` works.

**Where to start**
- Add `render_csv` to `domaincheck/report.py`, next to `render_json`.
- Add `"csv"` to the `--format` choices in `domaincheck/cli.py`.
- Add a test in `tests/test_checks.py` like `test_markdown_and_json_render`, including a detail that contains a comma.

candidates.title: [cli] Add --output csv/markdown formats
candidates.body:
## Problem
`swecc-oss explore` supports `--json` (raw GitHub objects) but nothing in between. People piping into `jq`, importing into spreadsheets, or pasting results into Discord need friendlier formats.

## Task
Add an `--output` option supporting `table` (default), `json` (slimmed-down objects: repo, number, title, labels, url, created, comments), `csv`, and `markdown`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `swecc-oss explore --output csv > issues.csv` opens cleanly in a spreadsheet
- [ ] `--output markdown` renders a copy-pasteable table for READMEs/Discord
- [ ] `--json` remains supported (consider making it an alias of `--output json`, deprecating gently)
- [ ] New formats covered by tests

## Files to look at
`src/swecc_oss_explorer/cli.py` (`explore` command), `tests/`
